chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

Some of the family of Zurarah asked him about a man who cut off the tongue of a mute man. He said: If his mother gave birth to him mute, then the diyyah is due upon him; but if his tongue was lost due to pain or an affliction after he had been speaking, then the one who cut it off owes one-third of the diyyah of his tongue.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money or financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.بِوَجَعٍ أَوْ آفَةٍ: due to illness, pain, or affliction that caused loss of speech
key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَةِ لِسَانِهِ: one-third of the prescribed compensation for his tongue
key_terms.لِسَانَ رَجُلٍ أَخْرَسَ: the tongue of a mute man, the specific injury discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for cutting the tongue of a person who is mute?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the diyyah for cutting the tongue of a mute person. It distinguishes between one born mute, for whom full diyyah applies, and one who became mute later through illness or affliction, for whom one-third of the tongue’s diyyah is due.
